item.title: Authorities investigating whether first Kenya and Nigeria Ebola cases crossed paths
item.description: Nigeria this week recorded its first case of Ebola in the current outbreak, which has spread from the epicenter in Congo to several other African countries.

item.title: Military reinforcements move to Mideast. And, millions of Americans vote early
item.description: Military reinforcements are heading to the Middle East and some personnel have left the region, pointing to a potential attack on Iran. And, millions of Americans have already voted in the midterms.

item.title: Retired general discusses the U.S. and Israeli plan for possible attack on Iran
item.description: NPR'S Leila Fadel speaks with retired four-star Gen. Joseph Votel about the war in Iran and the U.S. and Israeli objectives for a potential post-election bombing campaign.

item.title: Israel orders closure of West Bank after soldiers kill 2 men behind an alleged attack
item.description: Israeli soldiers shot and killed two men who the military said had launched an attack near the city of Hebron in the occupied West Bank on Friday morning. At least five people were injured, including some critically.

item.title: Europe's heat claims 50,000 lives. Climate change blamed for two-thirds of deaths
item.description: Blistering record heat in Europe this summer helped kill more than 50,000 people, with nearly two-thirds of that death toll blamed on human-caused climate change, a new study found.

item.title: Greetings from the Brazil-Argentina border, where waterfalls are flowing at near-record rates
item.description: The Iguazú Falls span more than a mile across both countries. A rain-soaked October, which scientists link to the Super El Niño, has sent near-record volumes of water surging over the towering cliffs.
